note: Current implementation status, 2026-11-19: tools/analytics_server.py implements the five defined events. Public events EV-01..03 persist as daily aggregates only when self-hosted; the committed GitHub Pages configuration is disabled because static hosting cannot accept POST requests. EV-04/05 require authorized first-party exports and never fire from the browser. Prior status text is retained in history_note, not presented as current.

principles.rule: No personal data, no cookie, no cross-site identifier, and no identifier derived from a visitor.
principles.why: Amazon's Participation Requirements forbid associating a sub-tag or reporting ID with a specific end user (R-08 in ledger/compliance.json; S02 in ledger/sources.json). A design that cannot do that even if asked is stronger than a policy that says not to.

principles.rule: Measure the page and the link, never the person.
principles.why: The only questions this site needs answered are 'which page sends people to which product' and 'which page earns'. Both are aggregate counts on a page-plus-link key. Nothing about an individual changes any decision the owner can make.

principles.rule: Publish no traffic, conversion or income expectation, and no forecast.
principles.why: The Operating Agreement states that Amazon makes no representation or warranty regarding the amount of traffic or commission income an Associate can expect (S58). A projection on this site would present as knowledge exactly what that clause disclaims. The layer records what happened; it never prints what will.

principles.rule: Every event has a stated decision it supports, or it is not collected.
principles.why: Measurement without a decision is cost with no benefit. This file therefore lists the decision beside each event, and the gate refuses an event with no decision.

principles.rule: Search measurement must not route visitors straight to Amazon.
principles.why: Search results, paid or unpaid, must send users to the site and not directly or indirectly to an Amazon Site (S51). Any Search Console or paid-search plan is constrained by that.

events.name: page_view
events.collected_by: assets/js/events.js + tools/analytics_server.py, when self-hosted with an explicit same-origin configuration
events.persistence: Daily aggregate SQLite counters; 90-day retention; no browser storage. Production GitHub Pages config disabled; no production collection claimed.
events.fires_on: A registered page loads in a browser with collection explicitly enabled and no GPC/DNT or automation exclusion.
events.decides: Which registered pages generated raw load events during the measured period. Use with query evidence and editorial judgment, not as proof of unique readers or demand.
events.analogy_in_repo: Implemented in tools/analytics_server.py and assets/js/events.js; see docs/MEASUREMENT.md.
events.blocked_by: An owner-controlled HTTPS collector/reverse proxy is not provisioned. The local service is implemented and tested; production is not connected.

events.name: product_link_click
events.collected_by: assets/js/events.js + tools/analytics_server.py, when self-hosted with an explicit same-origin configuration
events.persistence: Daily aggregate SQLite counters; 90-day retention; no browser storage. Production GitHub Pages config disabled; no production collection claimed.
events.fires_on: A click on a product link, before navigation.
fields: product_key P1..P5, never derived from a person
deliberately_not_collected: whether the visitor bought anything (the site cannot know this and must not imply it does)
events.decides: Which static product links generated raw click events. Counts can guide investigation, but do not establish purchase intent, attribution or a tested winner.
events.analogy_in_repo: Implemented in tools/analytics_server.py and assets/js/events.js; see docs/MEASUREMENT.md.
events.blocked_by: An owner-controlled HTTPS collector/reverse proxy is not provisioned. The local service is implemented and tested; production is not connected.

events.name: disclosure_view
events.collected_by: assets/js/events.js + tools/analytics_server.py, when self-hosted with an explicit same-origin configuration
events.persistence: Daily aggregate SQLite counters; 90-day retention; no browser storage. Production GitHub Pages config disabled; no production collection claimed.
events.fires_on: At least half the disclosure strip intersects the viewport, only when collection is enabled and IntersectionObserver is available.
events.decides: Whether at least half of the disclosure strip entered a browser viewport. This does not prove reading, legal compliance, or ordering relative to a click because no visitor/session sequence is stored.
events.analogy_in_repo: Implemented in tools/analytics_server.py and assets/js/events.js; see docs/MEASUREMENT.md.
events.blocked_by: An owner-controlled HTTPS collector/reverse proxy is not provisioned. The local service is implemented and tested; production is not connected.

events.name: conversion_import
events.fires_on: A manual or scheduled import of the Associates reporting CSV for a period.
deliberately_not_collected: any per-customer data - Associates reporting is aggregate by design
any value this project could compute but Amazon does not publish
events.decides: What the authorized aggregate report states for its tracking ID and period. It cannot assign orders to a particular page unless the actual authorized report/mapping establishes that breakdown.
events.blocked_by: The supplied tag is configured, but no authorized Associates reporting export or account-level destination/tracking validation is available in this workspace.
events.analogy_in_repo: tools/validate_data.py already forbids a populated clicks/conversion/earnings field anywhere in ledger/. This event is the only route by which those fields could ever legally be filled.
events.persistence: Authorized normalized CSV importer is implemented; no real export has been supplied or imported.

events.name: search_query_import
events.fires_on: A periodic export from Search Console.
deliberately_not_collected: personal information identified during the required human export review; a conservative automatic backstop is additional filtering, not a reliable name/address detector
events.decides: Which queries and pages have reported impressions/clicks in an authorized export. Data can inform a proposal; it does not by itself justify a popularity claim, profitable-niche ranking or automatic publication.
events.blocked_by: DQ-04: Search Console requires the owner's Google account and a verified property.
events.analogy_in_repo: marketing/trending-topics.html already argues that no topic on this site can be called trending without data. This event is what would make that possible.
events.persistence: Authorized normalized CSV importer is implemented; no real export has been supplied or imported.

decisions_enabled.rule: Compare raw page-load and product-click event counts only after collection exists. These are not unique visitors or eligible sessions; search impressions require EV-05.

decisions_enabled.decision: Which of the five products merits further research
decisions_enabled.rule: Use raw product-link event counts as one diagnostic after collection and data quality are reviewed. A higher count alone does not justify a superiority claim or a new article.

decisions_enabled.decision: Whether the disclosure is placed well enough
decisions_enabled.rule: Use aggregate visibility events as a layout diagnostic only. Without per-person sequences, this counter cannot establish whether an individual saw the disclosure before clicking. Manually and automatically inspect placement separately.

decisions_enabled.decision: Whether to change the content strategy at all
decisions_enabled.rule: Use only authorized report-derived outcomes in their actual scope, alongside query evidence and data-quality review. No access/report is supplied here; do not infer account existence, eligible Sessions, order totals or revenue.

privacy_and_consent.position: The implementation uses no browser storage, cookies, visitor identifiers, IP persistence, or full referrers. It honors Global Privacy Control and Do Not Track. This is an engineering minimization choice, not an exemption from privacy or consent law.
privacy_and_consent.what_is_asserted: Only properties enforced by the implementation and tests. GitHub and any reverse proxy may independently process addresses; configure and disclose host-level processing separately.
privacy_and_consent.what_is_not_asserted: No claim is made about GDPR, CCPA or any specific jurisdiction's requirements, and none should be inferred from this file. Whether a cookie-free aggregate counter falls inside or outside a particular regime is a legal question the owner must put to their own adviser. Recorded as a gap, not an answer.

open_items.item: Self-hosted collector implemented and tested, but no owner-controlled production HTTPS endpoint/reverse proxy is provisioned. GitHub Pages is static; production config remains disabled.
Implemented default: 90-day rolling retention, purged on ingestion/export and by a scheduled purge command. Confirm hosting logs, lawful basis and operator notice before production activation.

Basic automation exclusion in the client and a global request budget in the service are implemented. Origin validation is not human authentication; sophisticated bots can still inflate counts. No unique-human, session, or conversion-rate claim is made.
There is no way to verify a click led to a purchase from this side, and this project must never imply there is. Attribution is Amazon's to report, not this site's to guess.

history_note: T40 measurement layer - DATA MODEL AND DECISION PLAN. This file is a proposal, not an implementation. It defines what could be measured on this site, what may be measured under the program rules, and what each measurement would let the owner decide - so that the choice in discovery/suggestions.html DS-11 can be made against a concrete design instead of an idea. NOTHING here collects anything today: there is no script, no endpoint, no cookie and no account. The `status` of every event is DESIGNED, never LIVE, and the measurement gate fails the build if that ever changes without a recorded owner decision. UPDATE 2026-11-17 (session 7264f3c2): the owner recorded that decision on DS-11 and chose option A. EV-01, EV-02 and EV-03 are now LIVE as a privacy-preserving client-side counter (assets/js/events.js): no cookie, no identifier, nothing per person, and no count is published anywhere on the site. The events queue in the visitor's own browser only, because the endpoint that would persist them does not exist on GitHub Pages static hosting (MI-01 stays open). EV-04 and EV-05 remain BLOCKED on first-party reports. The wording above is kept for the record.
